dedupe_keys.name: walking access to hospitals in formal and informal areas of 19 sub saharan african cities

description: This study by John Friesen, Stefanos Georganos and Jan Haas (Communications Medicine, 2025) measures walking access to healthcare facilities in formal and informal residential areas of 19 sub-Saharan African cities. Coverage: open land use data for the 19 cities, regional healthcare facility locations and OpenStreetMap street networks, used to compute walking service areas around hospitals for travel times from 1 to 120 minutes, which are then combined with WorldPop population data. Across the cities, 33% of the urban population can reach a hospital within 15 minutes on foot, 58% within 30 minutes and 78% within 60 minutes; in some cities people in informal areas are clearly disadvantaged, most of all in medium-sized cities. Format and access: an open access journal article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: walking speeds are uniform and the facility list may be incomplete, so access in practice may differ. The service-area method and results can be used to test how pedestrian network disruptions, such as floods, change access to critical facilities in simulations. It relates to OpenStreetMap, WorldPop and Healthsites.io in the catalogue.
